headline: June Aster inquiry turns on blocked decks
deck: Reuters and ABC Australia report that survivors described two explosions before the MV June Aster burned; Reuters says investigators still cannot reach flooded lower decks and the engine room.
body: The MV June Aster inquiry now rests on two stubborn physical facts: survivors described explosions before the ferry burned, and investigators still cannot reach the flooded spaces most likely to hold direct evidence. Reuters reported that a Philippine Maritime Industry Authority statement cited survivor accounts of two explosions shortly before the fire; ABC Australia also reported MARINA's account of two successive explosions inside the vessel. [E1] [E3]

Access is still the mechanical limit on the case. Reuters reported that investigators probing the fire had not reached the flooded lower decks and engine room, so the public record can identify an investigative lead but not the failed part or point of origin. [E1]

The casualty count is now independently reported outside the Reuters update. AP reported on Sept. 12 that recovery of additional remains from the MV June Aster brought the toll to 76 dead with 13 missing. [E2]

What changes the inquiry next is not another theory about the blasts, but findings from the spaces investigators still cannot inspect and a fuller account of what survivors heard and where they were. Until then, the June Aster case remains an investigation around reported explosions rather than a settled finding about why the ferry burned. [E1] [E3]

evidence_box.fragment: Investigators probing the MV June Aster fire still cannot access flooded lower decks and the engine room; a Maritime Industry Authority statement cited survivor accounts reporting two explosions shortly before the fire. The recovery of 41 additional remains took the toll to 76 with 13 unaccounted for, and authorities said identification of heavily burned remains may take weeks or months.
